analysis.title: Global Equity Views, 4Q 2026
key_insights: JPMAM sees almost 30% global earnings growth this year and 20% in 2027, and says it has rarely seen such a strong profit cycle. The pace of upward revisions is cooling.

The US research team forecasts 27% operating profit growth this year, excluding mark-to-market gains on investments in companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The forecast was 13% at the start of the year and 26% in June, so it rose about 1 point in the last three months.

AI investment spending is the biggest profit driver and is still accelerating. The team expects robust spending well into 2028, but the market has already largely discounted another strong spending year in 2027.

Funding strain is appearing. Hyperscalers have increasingly turned to debt markets because spending now outstrips cash flow, and higher interest rates make borrowing costlier. Bonds and equities of some aggressive AI spenders, such as neocloud companies, have come under pressure.

The team revisited Robert Merton's 'distance to default' measure and says some of the stocks most under pressure in recent days look vulnerable. It remains constructive on AI but prefers higher quality names and is managing AI exposure and single-stock risk carefully.
Energy earnings are up over 80% this year. S&P 500 profit growth outside AI and energy is estimated at about 10% this year and next.
Almost 90% of S&P 500 companies are growing earnings, at the top of the historical range. This points to a wider set of opportunities for diversifying away from technology and AI exposure.

Valuations declined a little this year in most markets because profits rose faster than prices. Markets are seen as slightly expensive but not remarkably so. Higher US P/E multiples are viewed as justified by superior US profit growth.
Price/book ratios in emerging markets have rarely been this high, per the EM team. This reflects exceptional AI-driven profitability and shows downside risk if profit growth fades.
Chinese equity valuations look increasingly interesting after more underperformance. Software stocks, seen as 'AI losers', still offer good value despite a rally from recent lows.

Momentum was very strong across global equities over the past year and peaked in late June. In July momentum collapsed, with monthly performance in the bottom 1% over the last 100 years, which is unusual in a rising market.

Historically, prior momentum leaders recover modestly after a drawdown, while momentum laggards tend to perform very well. This supports a closer look at perceived AI losers, including software, where many may benefit from the new technology.

Japan has had more positive earnings surprises and forecast upgrades over the past five years than any other market. Drivers are renewed economic growth, rising prices, a weak yen helping exports, and better capital allocation, governance and profitability under government and TSE encouragement. Japan is presented as a diversifier.

The firm's investors are more neutral than positive on market returns. The recommendation is to stay invested and diversify by style and geography to manage AI concentration risk, with higher quality stocks seen as likely to deliver solid returns after underperformance.
The October 2026 survey of 48 CIOs and portfolio managers shows many favor industrials, financials, quality and select AI losers, and want to avoid consumer staples and leverage.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive on the AI theme with a strong preference for higher quality names, while managing overall AI and single-stock risk.
Seen as perceived AI losers but offering good value despite a rally, and many may benefit from AI adoption.
Earnings are up over 80% this year, described as exceptional profit growth. No explicit rating is given.
Many survey respondents name industrials among the best opportunities globally.
Many survey respondents name financials among the best opportunities globally.
Survey respondents favor avoiding consumer staples.

earnings_insights: JPMAM forecast: global earnings growth of almost 30% in 2026 and 20% in 2027 (forecast, no basis given).

JPMAM forecast: US operating profit growth of 27% in 2026, excluding mark-to-market gains on investments in Anthropic and OpenAI (forecast). The same forecast was 13% at the start of the year and 26% in June.
JPMAM estimate: S&P 500 profit growth outside AI and energy of about 10% annually in 2026 and 2027 (forecast).
Energy sector earnings are up over 80% in 2026 (JPMAM's wording, no basis stated).
Almost 90% of S&P 500 companies are growing earnings, near the top of the historical range.
risk_factors: Rising funding costs for AI spending as hyperscalers borrow because spending outstrips cash flow.
Pressure on bonds and equities of aggressive AI spenders such as neoclouds, with some stocks looking vulnerable on the distance to default measure.
Rising interest rates as a drag on profit growth outside the AI boom.
Concentration risk created by AI enthusiasm.
High emerging market price/book ratios leave downside if profit growth fades.
Survey-cited risks: politics, leverage, recession, rising rates, inflation, ORCL, market concentration, oil price.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares free cash flow for the hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) with the semiconductor names (Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom, Applied Materials), titled 'Hyperscalers' free cash flow has become semiconductors' free cash flow'.
Exhibit 2 shows semiconductors versus software relative performance over the past year, with labels 'Dec 31, 2025 to peak: 148%' and 'Peak to trough: -32%'.
Exhibit 3 shows JPMAM equity research cumulative expected return revision by region, with Japan's revisions outpacing the rest of the world over five years.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum factor performance in July 2026 ranked in the bottom 1% of monthly readings over the last 100 years, after a late-June peak in momentum.
Within tech, sentiment extremes between semiconductors and software have cooled, per the Exhibit 2 title.
Survey respondents name politics, leverage, recession, rising rates, inflation, ORCL, market concentration and oil price among the biggest risks to markets.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment is still accelerating, robust spending is expected well into 2028, and the team stays constructive on AI with a preference for higher quality names.
tension_points.bear_case: Spending outstrips cash flow, hyperscalers are turning to debt markets, borrowing costs are higher, and bonds and equities of aggressive spenders such as neoclouds are under pressure.

theme_stances.key_argument: Massive AI investment spending is the biggest profit driver and is still accelerating, though funding costs bear watching.
theme_stances.evidence: Massive AI investment spending is clearly the biggest driver

theme_stances.key_argument: Momentum laggards tend to perform very well after a momentum meltdown, and software still offers good value.
theme_stances.evidence: the laggards from the momentum phase tend to perform very well

theme_stances.key_argument: Japan has had more positive surprises and forecast upgrades than anywhere else over five years, and offers diversification.
theme_stances.evidence: more positive surprises and reasons to raise our forecasts in Japan
